figures_added.what: Cinema seating plan drawn as three rows of seats (row 1 = 5, row 2 = 7, row 3 = 9), growing by 2. Counts drawn match the opener boxes (7 and 9) and the derived rule 2n+3. SCREEN bar at top, seat counts labelled at the row ends.

Three dot patterns (pattern 1 = 3 dots, pattern 2 = 5, pattern 3 = 7) making a GCSE growing-pattern sequence concrete. Dots drawn match the stated counts; the walk derives d=2, zero term 1, rule 2n+1, pattern 10 = 21.

notes: Every bank problem is a numeric sequence (sequences given as numbers, not as printed patterns), so per the exam-realism test no bank problem prints a figure and none was added, matching the AQA sibling. Figures were added where the exam WOULD print one: the opener (cinema seating) and the bronze teach walk (dot pattern). Both SVGs are generated programmatically from their own numbers, self-contained, theme-safe (currentColor strokes and text, soft fills at 0.3 opacity: #60a5fa screen, #f59e0b seats, #34d399 dots), no external refs, Inter labels, under the size budget (opener ~3.5KB, teach ~2.2KB display strings). Every visible number was cross-checked against the walk/opener numbers. Figures were built into the guided conversion in one pass, so this shard is identical to the guided shard.
